plain: False statements that harm a person's good name

webster.text: The uttering of slanderous words with a view to injure another's reputation; the malicious uttering of falsehood respecting another which tends to destroy or impair his good name, character or occupation; slander; calumny.

example.quote: insomuch, that whatever violated either, throws down the sanctuary which covers the others, and that libels, falsehood, and defamation, equally with heresy and false religion, are withheld from the cognizance of federal tribunals.
example.cite: Thomas Jefferson, Draft of the Kentucky Resolutions, Oct. 1798
